subject.title: [Feature]: Optimization for Dockerfile.sandbox-common # add retries and fix-missings for apt-get

question: Should the sandbox Dockerfile fix be retry-only, or should OpenClaw intentionally accept `--fix-missing` partial-install semantics for these images?
rationale: `Acquire::Retries` directly addresses transient APT fetch failures, while `--fix-missing` changes required package failure behavior and needs an explicit owner decision before landing.

options.title: Use retry-only APT installs
options.body: Keep `Acquire::Retries=5` for network resilience and remove `--fix-missing` so required sandbox packages still fail closed after retries.

options.title: Accept partial-install behavior
options.body: Keep `--fix-missing` only if maintainers intentionally want builds to proceed after missing packages and add package-presence verification or documentation for that contract.

options.title: Pause for replacement
options.body: Leave the issue open and ask for a narrower replacement if the linked branch is not revised with proof.

recommendation.title: Use retry-only APT installs
recommendation.body: Keep `Acquire::Retries=5` for network resilience and remove `--fix-missing` so required sandbox packages still fail closed after retries.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Docker cache and sandbox-common setup history makes this the strongest routing candidate for the retry-versus-fix-missing decision.
